finding.claim: The icon URL is stored unvalidated in update() and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync() via a GET request (blind SSRF).
finding.source: icon parameter of Profile.update(String webhook, String icon), reachable via PUT /profile (src/Profile.java:11)

trace.note: update(String webhook, String icon) accepts icon from the request
this.iconUrl = icon; stores the value with no scheme, host, port, or private-address validation
nightly sync(HttpClient c) runs later as a second-order consumer of the stored value
URI.create(iconUrl) builds the request URL from the stored, attacker-controlled value
c.send issues the GET from the job's network position; the body is read into a byte array and discarded

finding.guards_checked: No validation on the icon path. The only check in the file is the webhook regex at line 12, which does not cover icon. The webhook path (line 12 regex, full-match via String.matches, fixed host hooks.example.com, alphanumeric path only, no userinfo) was checked and is SAFE. Redirect policy of the HttpClient passed in is not visible in this repo and was not assessed. Route auth for PUT /profile is not in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. src/Profile.java:12 (full-match webhook regex) applies only to webhook, not icon. Line 16 stores icon unchecked, and line 23 passes it straight to URI.create and c.send.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches src/Profile.java: update() takes icon at line 11, stores it unchecked at line 16, and sync() at lines 23-24 issues a GET to URI.create(iconUrl). No guard touches icon. The residual uncertainty is outside this repo: the PUT /profile auth and the caller-supplied HttpClient's redirect policy are not visible, though the default HttpClient does not follow redirects.
